overview: This lesson introduces Class 4 students to the concept of the water cycle, explaining how water continuously moves on, above, and below the Earth's surface. Students will learn about the key stages of evaporation, condensation, and precipitation, and understand their importance in making water available. The lesson emphasizes the cyclical nature of water's journey and its relevance to everyday life.
objectives: [Remember] Identify the three main stages of the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
[Understand] Describe how water changes state and moves through the different stages of the water cycle.
[Apply] Give examples of where evaporation occurs (e.g., from oceans, rivers, plants) and where precipitation falls (e.g., as rain on land or into oceans).
[Understand] Explain that the water cycle is a continuous process that ensures water is available on Earth.

activities.title: Where does the water go?
activities.description: Begin by asking students to think about everyday observations: 'What happens to puddles after it rains?' 'Where does the steam from a hot cup of tea go?' 'How do wet clothes dry?' Introduce the idea of water changing and moving.

activities.title: Water on the Move - Diagram Study
activities.description: Display a large, simplified diagram of the water cycle. Ask students to identify elements they recognize (e.g., sun, clouds, ocean, rain, rivers). Guide them to observe the arrows showing movement.

activities.title: The Water Cycle Journey
activities.description: The teacher explains the three main stages: Evaporation (water turning into vapour from oceans, rivers, land, and plants/transpiration), Condensation (vapour forming clouds), and Precipitation (water falling back as rain, snow, etc., to land or ocean). Briefly mention surface runoff and water seeping into the ground (groundwater). Highlight that oceans cover a significant part of Earth and are a major source of evaporation.

activities.title: Label the Cycle
activities.description: Provide each student with a pre-printed blank water cycle diagram. Students will label the main stages and processes discussed (e.g., Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Ocean, Cloud, River).

activities.title: Quick Check
activities.description: Teacher asks a few quick questions to assess understanding.

assessment:
1. Name the three main stages of the water cycle.
2. Describe what happens during evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
3. Give two examples of where water evaporates from and two examples of where precipitation falls.
4. Why is the continuous movement of water through the water cycle important for us?
